messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] illness-death model with recovery
messages.body_plain:
Dear R-Epi users;i am trying to fit an illness-death model with recovery using both Epi (version 0.9.6) and coxph but my results are not similar. When fitting a time to death model and all other states censored I get equivalent results. I think I am doing everything right and can't really think of a mistake on my part unless I am missing something in Epi for multistate models.This is how I set up the Epi data:msm.lexis.dta <- Lexis(    entry=list(per=start),    exit=list(per=stop),    entry.status=from,     exit.status=to,     id=case,    data=msm2b)with(msm.lexis.dta, table(from,to))msm.lexis.glm <- splitLexis(msm.lexis.dta,    breaks=quantile(c(0,msm.lexis.dta$stop),probs=seq(0,1,by=1/10)),    time.scale="per")for(i in 1:2){    for(j in 1:3){        if(i != j){            cat("from ==",i,"to ==",j,"
")            cat("Cox proportional hazards
")            h.rate <- coxph(Surv(time=start,time2=stop,event=(to==j))~sex+age,data=subset(msm.lexis.dta,from==i))            print(round(ci.lin(h.rate, Exp=TRUE), 3));cat("
");            cat("Poisson regression
")            h.rate <- glm(as.numeric(to==j)~ns(per)+sex+age+offset(log(lex.dur)),                family=poisson,data=subset(msm.lexis.glm,from==i))            print(round(ci.lin(h.rate, Exp=TRUE), 3));cat("
");        }    }}And the answers I get for my data are:from == 1 to == 2Cox proportional hazards          Estimate StdErr      z     P exp(Est.)  2.5% 97.5%sexFemale    0.084  0.141  0.594 0.553     1.088 0.824 1.435age         -0.001  0.008 -0.099 0.921     0.999 0.983 1.015Poisson regression            Estimate StdErr       z     P exp(Est.)  2.5% 97.5%(Intercept)   -0.176  0.154  -1.141 0.254     0.839 0.620 1.135ns(per)       -4.524  0.315 -14.379 0.000     0.011 0.006 0.020sexFemale     -0.085  0.079  -1.073 0.283     0.919 0.787 1.073age            0.003  0.004   0.626 0.531     1.003 0.994 1.012from == 1 to == 3Cox proportional hazards          Estimate StdErr      z     P exp(Est.)  2.5% 97.5%sexFemale    0.208  0.213  0.977 0.329     1.232 0.811 1.871age         -0.007  0.013 -0.553 0.580     0.993 0.968 1.018Poisson regression            Estimate StdErr      z     P exp(Est.)  2.5% 97.5%(Intercept)   -1.608  0.378 -4.252 0.000     0.200 0.095 0.420ns(per)       -5.893  0.855 -6.895 0.000     0.003 0.001 0.015sexFemale      0.265  0.182  1.456 0.145     1.304 0.912 1.863age           -0.008  0.011 -0.712 0.476     0.992 0.971 1.014Kind regards, Vumani

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Epi 1.0.7 now out
messages.body_plain:
Dear R-sig-Epi list,

We have now made a major update of the Epi package, to version 1.0.7.
It has just appeared on CRAN.

For a few days the version 1.0.5 was there, but there were grave bugs
in splitLexis and cutLexis, so please update to 1.0.7 if you have the
1.0.5. ( Use: installed.packages()["Epi","Version"] to check ).

The biggest change since the previous version 0.7.0 on CRAN is the
introduction of a new machinery for representation of follow-up data
through the Lexis() function that creates a Lexis object. It enables
simultaneous representation of follow-up on different timescales and
also representation of multistate data, i.e. transitions between
several different states (not only alive -> dead). Time-splitting of
follow-up data is done with the functions splitLexis(), cutLexis() and
countLexis(). Overview of multistate data is given by tab.Lexis().

Included in the package is a vignette explaining this machinery in
detail --- start the html-help (write help.start() at the command
prompt) and at the front page for the Epi package, click on a link in
"Read overview or browse directory".

Note that the old Lexis()-function (by David Clayton) is dead. It is
still in the package, but now under the name W.Lexis(). Its
functionality, splitting follow-up time, is taken over by
splitLexis().

The function epi.eff() is replaced by effx() and effx.match().

Enjoy!

Best wishes,
Bendix Carstensen,
maintainer of Epi

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] standard errors from Icens function
messages.body_plain:
I am using the Icens function to do a survival analysis of interval censored
data.  The article referenced for this function (Carstensen 1996) says that
standard errors for the parameter estimates using this method with packages
such as GLIM are incorrect because they are based on the expected
information.  Are the standard errors output in the R function incorrect as
well?
Thanks,
Summer
